metadata.title: KMU MDCAT 2025 — Paper D
metadata.description: Paper D · 180 original MCQs · provisional chapter and topic classifications

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Intrinsic factor secreted by parietal cells is essential for:
options: Absorption of vitamin B12 in the intestine
Neutralization of stomach acid in the duodenum
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Absorption of vitamin B12 in the intestine”. This tests human digestion & absorption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Delta D cells in the islets of Langerhans secrete:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Somatostatin”. This tests general concepts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the main function of duodenum:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Digestion of food”. This tests human digestion & absorption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which stage of the swallowing process prevents food or liquid from being aspirated to the lungs?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Pharyngeal”. This tests respiration & gas transport.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which type of nephron is responsible for the development of osmotic gradients in the renal medulla?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Juxtamedullary”. This tests kidney & osmoregulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following best describes how the distal convoluted tubule contributes to regulation of blood pH in the body?
options: Active secretion of hydrogen ions into the filtrate
Active secretion of sodium from the glomerular filtrate
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Active secretion of hydrogen ions into the filtrate”. This tests general concepts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The sodium potassium pumps in the distal convoluted tubule are activated by:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Aldosterone”. This tests kidney & osmoregulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If a person drinks excessive amount of water, how does the kidney respond to maintaining osmoregulation?
options: Increase ADH release and water reabsorption
Increase aldosterone release and reabsorb more sodium
Decrease ADH release and increase water excretion
Decrease renin secretion and retain more water
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Decrease ADH release and increase water excretion”. This tests kidney & osmoregulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primary function of glomerular capillaries is:
options: Reabsorption of water and solutes from the renal tubules
Secretion of waste products from the blood into the tubules
Filtration of blood from glomerular filtrate
Supply of nutrients and oxygen to the kidney tissue
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Filtration of blood from glomerular filtrate”. This tests kidney & osmoregulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a heat stroke the hypothalamus will detect an increase in core body temperature, which of the following response is triggered?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Vasodilation and sweating”. This tests nervous system & reflexes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which nitrogenous waste has the lowest solubility in water?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Uric acid”. This tests kidney & osmoregulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: By nature, human excretory system is:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Ureotelic”. This tests kidney & osmoregulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hyperparathyroidism may lead to the formation of:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Calcium phosphate stones”. This tests general concepts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In somatic cell hybridization, which two cells are fused to produce monoclonal antibodies?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “B-lymphocytes and spleen cells”. This tests heart, blood & lymphatic system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In molecular diagnostics, the primary function of DNA/RNA probes is to:
options: Replace malfunctioning genes in effected cells
Bind to specific DNA or RNA sequences for identification
Cut genetic material at precise locations
Stimulate immune responses against disease- causing organisms
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Bind to specific DNA or RNA sequences for identification”. This tests dna technology & medical applications.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A set of uniform proteins generated by genetically identical immune cells are:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Monoclonal antibodies”. This tests immune responses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which biotechnological product is used to replace an abnormal gene in a patient's cells?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Vector”. This tests general concepts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Watson and Crick's DNA model, which of the following pairs with Cytosine?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Guanine”. This tests macromolecules & their properties.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fats are considered as a very efficient source of energy because they:
options: Produce ATP directly and without requiring respiration
Enter into glycolysis without any modification
Generate multiple acetyl groups that produce more ATP
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Generate multiple acetyl groups that produce more ATP”. This tests cellular respiration & atp.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The junction between two consecutive neurons where information is transmitted from one neuron to the next is called:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Synapse”. This tests nervous system & reflexes.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Cellular respiration”. This tests respiration & gas transport.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which ion is tenfold higher in concentration outside the membrane of neuron during resting potential?

questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Shaking hands with infected person”. This tests classification of viruses & transmission.

It changes the shape of the enzyme

questions.subject: Biology

questions.question: The number of chromosomes in a haploid cell are:
options: Half the chromosomes in a normal body cell
Double the chromosomes in a normal body cell
Quarter the chromosomes in a normal body cell
Equal to the chromosomes in a normal body cell

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Living cells Do NOT directly acquire energy released from the breakdown of food molecules inside the cells because:
options: Glucose cannot be broken down by the cells
Energy released is too small to be used by the cells
Glucose molecules do not store any energy
The energy released is too large, leading to heating and wastage
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “The energy released is too large, leading to heating and wastage”. This tests human digestion & absorption.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which properties of water enable it to circulate in living bodies and act as transport medium?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Adhesion and cohesion”. This tests heart, blood & lymphatic system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A scientist cuts the tails of mice for several generations, but their offspring are always born with tails. This rejects:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Lamarckism”. This tests evolutionary theories.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How are the phospholipid molecules arranged in the plasma membrane?
options: Hydrophilic heads face inwards and hydrophobic tails face outwards
Both Hydrophilic heads face each other in the membrane
Hydrophilic heads face outwards and hydrophobic tails face inwards
Hydrophilic heads and hydrophobic tails are randomly distributed
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Hydrophilic heads face outwards and hydrophobic tails face inwards”. This tests macromolecules & their properties.

questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Ribose - Pentose, Aldehyde group”. This tests macromolecules & their properties.

options: Receptor, associative neuron, sensory neuron, motor neuron, effector
Receptor, motor neuron, associative neuron, sensory neuron, effector
Receptor, sensory neuron, associative neuron, motor neuron, effector
Receptor, sensory neuron, motor neuron, associative neuron, effector

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of Mendel's laws can best explain why a child may inherit brown eyes even if one parent has blue eyes?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Law of Dominance”. This tests chromosomes & mendelian genetics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the significance of the 9:3:3:1 ratio in a dihybrid cross?
options: It proves that all genes are linked
It demonstrates that traits assort independently
It confirms that mutations have occurred
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “It demonstrates that traits assort independently”. This tests chromosomes & mendelian genetics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In crossing over, an exchange of maternal and paternal chromatid parts occurs while homologous chromosomes are paired during _____ stage of meiosis.
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Prophase I”. This tests chromosomes & mendelian genetics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Linked genes DO NOT follow Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment because _____.
options: They are located on different chromosomes
They are physically close together on the same chromosome
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “They are physically close together on the same chromosome”. This tests chromosomes & mendelian genetics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A carrier female for an X-linked recessive disorder:
options: Cannot pass the disorder to offspring
Can pass the disorder to her sons
Only passes the disorder to daughters
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Can pass the disorder to her sons”. This tests chromosomes & mendelian genetics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an X-Linked recessive disorder in humans?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Hemophilia”. This tests chromosomes & mendelian genetics.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following CORRECTLY describes the expected outcome of children from a carrier mother for haemophilia (XʰX) and a normal father (XY)?
options: 50% of sons will be hemophilic, and 50% of daughters will be carriers
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “50% of sons will be hemophilic, and 50% of daughters will be carriers”. This tests chromosomes & mendelian genetics.

questions.subject: Biology

questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Pericardium”. This tests heart, blood & lymphatic system.

questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Ventricular systole”. This tests heart, blood & lymphatic system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic: Cardiac Cycle and Phases of Heartbeat
questions.question: Which part of the heart's conducting system delays the impulse from atria to the ventricles?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Atrio-ventricular node”. This tests nervous system & reflexes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic: Cardiac Cycle and Phases of Heartbeat
questions.question: The heartbeat sound "LUB" is produced on closure of:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Atrio-ventricular valves”. This tests heart, blood & lymphatic system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the primary function of lymphatic vessels?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Drain excess interstitial fluid”. This tests heart, blood & lymphatic system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primary role of helper T-cells in immune response is:
options: Secreting perforins to destroy target cells
Assisting B-cells and other T-cells in their function
Inhibiting over activity of the immune system
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Assisting B-cells and other T-cells in their function”. This tests immune responses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Identify the primary characteristic of 3rd line of defense.
options: Specific recognition and memory of pathogens
General inflammation at the site of infection
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Specific recognition and memory of pathogens”. This tests nervous system & reflexes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following best describes Inspiratory Reserve Volume (IRV)?
options: The volume of air forcibly exhaled after normal tidal volume
The volume of air remaining in the lungs after forcible expiration
The volume of air exchanged during normal breathing
The volume of air forcibly inhaled after normal tidal volume
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “The volume of air forcibly inhaled after normal tidal volume”. This tests respiration & gas transport.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During gaseous exchange in human respiration, enzyme carbonic anhydrase is directly involved in the:
options: Combination of water with carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Combination of water with carbon dioxide”. This tests respiration & gas transport.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What happens when the external intercostal muscles contract during inhalation in humans?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “The ribs move outward”. This tests muscles, bones & joints.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primary effect of smoking on the respiratory system:
options: Increased lung function due to presence of nicotine
Reduced risk of lung cancer due to tolerance
Damage to alveoli reducing gaseous exchange
Improves oxygenation of the blood by activating hemoglobin
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Damage to alveoli reducing gaseous exchange”. This tests respiration & gas transport.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Lenz's Law, the direction of induced current in a conductor is such that it:
options: Opposes the change in magnetic flux
Enhances the change in magnetic flux
Is perpendicular to the magnetic field
Is parallel to the magnetic field
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Opposes the change in magnetic flux”. This tests faraday & lenz laws.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a pure capacitance AC circuit, the current:

questions.question: In a full-wave rectifier using two diodes, the diodes D₁ and D₂ operate:

questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “In alternate switching mode”. This tests wave motion & interference.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The energy (E) of a quantum is given by which equation?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “E = hf”. This tests general concepts.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In the hydrogen spectrum, the Brackett series lies in:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Infrared region”. This tests general concepts.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statement best describes the nature of nuclear decay?
options: It occurs both spontaneously and randomly
It occurs only when external energy is supplied
It can be controlled by temperature and pressure
It occurs at regular time intervals for each atom
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “It occurs both spontaneously and randomly”. This tests nuclear & quantum physics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A boat moves 4 km east and then 3 km north. Another boat moves 3 km north first and then 4 km east. Which statement is CORRECT about their final displacements?
options: Both boats have the same displacement vector
The first boat's displacement is greater because it traveled east first
The second boat's displacement is greater because it travelled north first
Both boats end at different positions but cover the same distance
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Both boats have the same displacement vector”. This tests vector operations.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The area under the line on a displacement-time graph of a car moving with uniform velocity would be a:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Triangle”. This tests kinematics & dynamics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A car starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 3 m/s². What will be its velocity after 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “15 m/s”. This tests kinematics & dynamics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A passenger is standing in a stationary bus. When the bus suddenly starts moving forward, the passenger falls backward. Which phenomenon best explains this observation?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Inertia”. This tests wave motion & interference.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ball is projected at an angle 45° with an initial speed of 20 m/s on earth. How does Rᵥᵥ (Range with air resistance) compare to Rₐ (Range without air resistance)?
options: Rₐ will be greater than Rᵥᵥ because air resistance reduces horizontal speed
Rᵥᵥ will be equal to Rₐ because gravity is unchanged
Rₐ will be lesser than Rᵥᵥ because air resistance reduces horizontal speed
Rᵥᵥ will be lesser than Rₐ because air resistance random
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Rₐ will be lesser than Rᵥᵥ because air resistance reduces horizontal speed”. This tests resistance & electrical circuits.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A 0.02 kg bullet moving at 300 m/s embeds itself in a 2 kg block at rest on a smooth surface. What is velocity of the block-bullet system just after impact?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “3 m/s”. This tests kinematics & dynamics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following statement about projectile motion is CORRECT?
options: The horizontal velocity of a projectile changes constantly due to gravity
The vertical velocity of a projectile remains constant throughout the flight
At the highest point, the vertical velocity of the projectile is zero, but the horizontal velocity remains unchanged
The acceleration of the projectile is zero at the peak of its trajectory
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “At the highest point, the vertical velocity of the projectile is zero, but the horizontal velocity remains unchanged”. This tests kinematics & dynamics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The rate of doing work at any instant of time is called:
questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “Instantaneous power”. This tests work, power & energy.

questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “1470 J”. This tests work, power & energy.

Student B uses more power than student A
Both students do the same amount of work, but student A uses more power
Student A and B use the same power since they lifted the same weight

questions.explanation: The supplied answer key selects “2.4 m/s”. This tests angular & circular motion.

Perpendicular to the plane and pointing out of the page
Perpendicular to the plane and pointing into the page

questions.question: If a particle moves along a circular path of radius r with angular displacement θ (in radians), then the arc length s is given by:
